newsitem.title: INDIA: Strict vigil checks Tamil refugee inflow to India.
newsitem.headline: Strict vigil checks Tamil refugee inflow to India.

text.p: The number of Tamil refugees fleeing war-ravaged Sri Lanka for southern India has dropped as authorities in both countries step up boat patrols, police said on Sunday.
About 2,500 refugees have made the narrow crossing between the island nation and India's Tamil Nadu state since the influx began in July.
But Indian vessels belonging to the navy, coast guard and customs have seized 15 boats ferrying refugees, and the Sri Lankan navy has intercepted three, police in Tamil Nadu's capital Madras said.
"The realisation that seizure is not an empty threat has made both Sri Lankan Tamil and Indian boatmen wary of bringing refugees, however lucrative it might be," a senior police officer said.

Police say refugees pay 3,000 to 5,000 rupees ($85-$140) per person to be ferried across the 35-km (20-mile) stretch called the Palk strait. Relief workers in Madras estimate that as many as 100,000 Tamils may be waiting to flee to India.

Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. More than 50,000 people have been killed in the 13-year conflict.

With 50 million Tamil-speaking people, Tamil Nadu has provided a safe sanctuary for both Tamil residents and rebels since 1983. Some 200,000 refugees landed in Tamil Nadu in the 1980s. Many are still in camps.
But sympathy soured after the 1991 murder of former Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi by a suspected LTTE female suicide bomber during an election campaign in the state.
